title: Principal Salary NSW: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual pay for a principal salary in NSW. Includes tax, super, and the 38-hour week formula.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 then by 52, before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, assume 38 hours per week. For example, $50 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $98,800 per year. This is gross annual pay before tax, Medicare levy, and super. Use the timesheet on this site to do the calculation instantly.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage (from 1 July 2026: $26.44 per hour) is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are higher minimums set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries or occupations. Your principal salary in NSW may be above both, but always check the relevant award. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate (e.g., $33.05 per hour for minimum wage casuals).

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. If your base rate is $30 per hour, casual loading adds $7.50, making your total $37.50 per hour. Super is calculated on the base rate plus casual loading. When using the timesheet, check the casual loading box to include it. Do not type a rate that already includes casual loading.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Principal Salary in NSW

If you're negotiating a **principal salary in NSW**, you'll likely see offers expressed as an annual figure. But if you're paid by the hour—or you want to compare an hourly rate to a salary—you need a reliable conversion. This guide explains the formula, tax, super, and the key differences between minimum wage, award rates, and casual loading.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks.

For a standard full-time role, we assume **38 hours per week** (the ordinary hours under the Fair Work Act). For example:
- $60 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $118,560 per year.
- $80 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $158,080 per year.

This formula assumes you work the same hours every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. It's a starting point for estimating your **principal salary in NSW**.

### Why 38 Hours?

The 38-hour week is the standard for full-time employees in Australia. Some awards or agreements set different ordinary hours (e.g., 35 or 40), but 38 is the most common. If your role specifies a different figure, adjust the formula accordingly. For part-time or casual work, use your actual weekly hours.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. Using the example above: $60 per hour × 38 hours = $2,280 per week, so $4,560 per fortnight. This can help you budget between pay cycles.

## Tax and Medicare Levy on Your Annual Pay

Once you have your annual gross, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the **Medicare levy** of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a principal salary in NSW of $150,000, tax would be approximately $36,138 plus Medicare $3,000, leaving about $110,862 after tax (before super).

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a detailed breakdown.

### Super Guarantee

Your employer must pay super guarantee of **12%** on your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. For a $150,000 annual salary, that's an extra $18,000 contributed to your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional cost to your employer. When comparing a **principal salary in NSW** to an hourly rate, remember that super is paid on top of the hourly rate as well.

## Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

### National Minimum Wage

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is **$26.44 per hour** ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). This is the legal floor for employees not covered by an award. Casual workers get an extra 25% loading: **$33.05 per hour**.

### Award Rates

Most industries have award rates set by the Fair Work Commission, which are higher than the minimum wage. For example, the Professional Employees Award covers many principal-level roles. Always check the relevant award via [pay guides](/blog) or the Fair Work Ombudsman.

### Casual Loading

If you're a casual employee, your hourly rate includes a 25% loading to compensate for not receiving paid leave. When using our [the timesheet](/), check the casual loading box—do not enter a rate that already includes loading. The tool will add 25% on top of your base rate.

## Average Earnings in NSW

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (May 2026), full-time adult ordinary time earnings in New South Wales averaged **$2,108.80 per week** (approximately $109,657 per year). This is an average, not a median for any specific job. Your **principal salary in NSW** may be above or below this figure depending on your role, experience, and industry.

For all employees (including part-time), total average weekly earnings were $1,579.20. These figures help you benchmark, but they are not a substitute for your own rate.

## Using the Timesheet

Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and see annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. You can also toggle casual loading. Remember that the result is an estimate—always confirm with your employer or a payroll professional.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

## Next Steps

- Check your award or agreement for minimum rates.
- Use the [reference tables](/data) for tax and super thresholds.
- Read about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) to optimise your total package.

Understanding your **principal salary in NSW** starts with a clear conversion from hourly to annual. Use the formula, consider tax and super, and always verify with official sources.
